parameters.name: criterion
parameters.value: cells with fewer than 200 genes expressed and genes which are expressed in fewer than 200 cells

evidence.quote: We follow standard preprocessing steps for single-cell RNA seq data, including filtering cells with fewer than 200 genes expressed and filtering genes which are expressed in fewer than 200 cells.

decisions.rationale: R6: filtering cells and genes by stated criteria -> select.

parameters.name: criterion
parameters.value: over 2500 counts or greater than 20 percent of transcript counts from mitochondrial genes

evidence.quote: Quality control metrics are then calculated based on mitochondrial gene counts within each cell using the Scanpy Python library [48], and low-quality cells are filtered out which contain over 2500 counts, or which have greater than 20 percent of transcript counts from mitochondrial genes.

decisions.rationale: R6: quality-control filtering removes cells meeting stated thresholds -> select.

parameters.name: method
parameters.value: row-normalized so that each cell sums up to 10,000 transcript counts

evidence.quote: The count matrix is then row-normalized so that each cell sums up to 10,000 transcript counts and then log-normalized [49], obtaining the final preprocessed count matrix C ′ .

decisions.rationale: R6: row normalization to a stated per-cell total -> normalize.

evidence.quote: The count matrix is then row-normalized so that each cell sums up to 10,000 transcript counts and then log-normalized [49], obtaining the final preprocessed count matrix C ′ .

decisions.rationale: R6: stated log normalization -> log_transform.

evidence.quote: The Cell2Sentence transformation is at its core a reorganization of the cell expression matrix into sequences of gene names ordered by decreasing transcript abundance, similar to rank-ordering transformations of count matrices [44].
Wedenote the rank-order transformation applied on C ′ as S , and the sequence of gene names resulting from S ( C i ) as cell sentence s i for each cell i in the preprocessed count matrix.

decisions.rationale: R6: gene names are ordered by transcript abundance -> rank.

decisions.chain_element: attach biological metadata such as cell type, tissue, or disease

evidence.quote: Cell sentences may be annotated with biological metadata, such as cell type, tissue, or disease.

decisions.rationale: R6: metadata is attached to the textual cell sentence -> serialize.

evidence.quote: In order to limit computational costs, we truncate each cell sentence to only keep the 100 highest expressed (top 100 ranked) genes.

decisions.rationale: R6: retaining the top-N genes from a list -> select.
